name: Virunga National Park
subtitle: A natural property on the UNESCO World Heritage List since 1979.

facts.label: In Danger
facts.value: on UNESCO's List of World Heritage in Danger (since 1994)

parts.text: UNESCO describes the property in these words: “Virunga National Park (covering an area of 790,000 ha) comprises an outstanding diversity of habitats, ranging from swamps and steppes to the snowfields of Rwenzori at an altitude of over 5,000 m, and from lava plains to the savannahs on the slopes of volcanoes. Mountain gorillas are found in the park, some 20,000 hippopotamuses live in the rivers and birds from Siberia spend the winter there.”

Virunga National Park lies in the Albertine Rift in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, along the borders with Uganda and Rwanda. Wikipedia says it was created in 1925, covers 7,800 km² and ranges in height from 680 metres to 5,109 metres in the Rwenzori Mountains.

Two active volcanoes, Nyiragongo and Nyamuragira, lie within it. More than 3,000 species of animals and plants have been recorded, over 300 of them found only in the Albertine Rift, including the eastern gorilla and the golden monkey.
It was listed as a World Heritage Site in 1979 for its range of habitats, its biodiversity and its protection of rare mountain gorilla habitat.
